clues.text: This place sits on flat farm land in the center of its state, by a river. Roads from all sides cross here, so folks call it a crossroads.
clues.narrowing: Puts the player on a flat river plain at the center of its state, where roads cross.

source.quote: Indianapolis is situated in the state's central till plain region along the west fork of the White River. The city's official slogan, "Crossroads of America", reflects its historic importance as a transportation hub

clues.text: Spring days here can trick you badly. A warm day in March or April can end with snow falling just a day or two later.
clues.narrowing: Rules out steady climates; keeps a place where warm days flip to snow fast.

source.quote: Midday temperature drops exceeding 30 °F or 17 °C are common during March and April, and instances of very warm days (80 °F or 27 °C) followed within 36 hours by snowfall are not unusual during these months

clues.text: This place was planned from scratch in 1821 to be the new seat of government. Its streets were laid out in a neat grid on one square mile.
clues.narrowing: Shrinks the list to towns planned from scratch as a seat of government in 1821.

source.quote: In 1821, Indianapolis was established as a planned city for the new seat of Indiana's state government. The city was platted by Alexander Ralston and Elias Pym Fordham on a one-square-mile (2.6 km2) grid

clues.text: Each year this place hosts a famed car race known all around the world. It is the largest one-day sports event in the whole world.
clues.narrowing: Nearly decisive: one famed car race, the largest one-day sports event on Earth.

source.quote: The city's international reputation rests primarily on the Indianapolis 500, the world's largest single-day sporting event

clues.text: This place is the seat of government for Indiana. Its governor and its state lawmakers both work here.
clues.narrowing: Confirms it: the governor and the state lawmakers are based here.

source.quote: is the capital and most populous city of the U.S. state of Indiana

reveal.blurb: In 1816, the year its state was born, Congress set aside land in the center for a new seat of government. Builders laid out a planned town there in 1821, and the government moved in by 1825. Race cars now roar around its famed track each year. Indianapolis is the capital of Indiana.
